overview: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Urban Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NULM) is a centrally sponsored scheme launched by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs to reduce poverty and vulnerability of urban poor households by enabling access to self-employment and skilled wage employment opportunities. It aims to build strong grassroots-level institutions of the poor, provide shelter for the urban homeless, support street vendors, and promote financial inclusion and skill development. The mission operates through a three-tier structure at national, state, and city levels, with implementation led by Urban Local Bodies (ULBs).
objectives: Reduce poverty and vulnerability of urban poor households by enabling access to self-employment and skilled wage employment opportunities
Build strong grassroots level institutions of the poor through social mobilisation and institution development
Provide shelter equipped with essential services to the urban homeless in a phased manner
Facilitate access to suitable spaces, institutional credit, social security, and skills for urban street vendors
Ensure universal coverage of urban poor for skill development and credit facilities
Promote convergence with schemes of relevant line ministries and state governments
Encourage partnership with private sector for skill training, employment, and shelter operations
Cater to especially vulnerable segments such as dependent children, aged, disabled, mentally ill, and recovering patients
eligibility: The primary target of DAY-NULM is the urban poor, including the urban homeless. As an interim measure, the target is the urban population identified as below poverty line by States/UTs. Coverage may be broadened to include families of disadvantaged groups like SCs, STs, women, minorities, disabled, etc., subject to a maximum of 25 percent of the urban poor population. For Self-Employment Programme (SEP), no minimum educational qualification is required, but training must be provided if special skills are needed for the enterprise. For group enterprises under SEP, the group must have a minimum of 3 members (amended) with at least 70% from urban poor families, and no more than one person from the same family should be included. For Employment through Skills Training & Placement (EST&P), eligibility varies by training type: fresh entrants require minimum 200 hours, reskilling requires 16 hours, and formal recognition requires bridge courses if needed.
benefits: Benefits include access to skill training for market-based jobs and self-employment, interest subsidy on bank loans for individual and group enterprises (difference between 7% and prevailing rate), revolving fund support to Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and their federations, financial inclusion through basic savings accounts and credit linkage, shelter for urban homeless with basic infrastructure, identity cards and social security linkages for street vendors, training and stipend for street vendors, and support for innovative and special projects. Non-financial benefits include capacity building, institution formation, bank linkage, training of community organisers, and convergence with other government schemes for entitlements like food, healthcare, education, and housing.
financial_support: Financial support under DAY-NULM includes interest subsidy on bank loans for individual micro-enterprises (project cost up to Rs. 2 lakhs) and group enterprises (project cost up to Rs. 10 lakhs), where the subsidy covers the difference between 7% per annum and the prevailing interest rate, subject to timely repayment. For Self-Help Groups, revolving fund support is provided. Under convergence with PMFME, seed capital of Rs. 40,000 per SHG member is available for working capital and small tools, repayable as a loan from SHG federations at interest not exceeding 6% per annum. Credit-linked subsidy of 35% of project cost, up to Rs. 10 lakh, is available for food processing enterprises. Funding for City Livelihood Centres (CLCs) and shelters is also provided. The overall expenditure on Capacity Building and Training (CB&T) is capped at 12% of total allocation.
application_process: 1. Identify prospective beneficiaries through Community Organisers (COs) or ULB officials from urban poor households. 2. Submit application of intent with basic details (name, age, contact, address, Aadhaar, loan required, bank account, enterprise type) to ULB. 3. ULB enters details into a register or MIS and issues acknowledgement with unique registration number. 4. ULB screens applications and forwards recommended cases to Task Force at ULB level. 5. Task Force scrutinises applications, conducts interviews, and recommends or rejects based on viability. 6. Recommended cases are sent to concerned banks for processing within 15 days. 7. Banks process loans and submit periodic reports to ULB on application status. 8. For interest subsidy, banks submit quarterly claims to ULB after loan disbursement; ULB verifies and releases subsidy (difference between 7% and prevailing rate) to banks. 9. For SEP-G (group enterprises), similar process applies with group entry form and verification of group strength and urban poor membership. 10. For SHG bank linkage, SHGs apply through ULB, and subsidy is released on timely repayment. 11. For innovative projects, proposals are submitted to State/UT Government or SULM, screened by National Mission Directorate, and approved by Project Approval Committee (PAC).
required_documents: Declaration signed by SHG office bearers
Enterprise bank account copy (for group/activity group)
deadlines: Rolling basis — applications are accepted throughout the year.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India
caveats: Interest subsidy is released only on timely repayment of loan
For group enterprises under SEP, minimum 3 members required with at least 70% from urban poor families and no more than one person from the same family
Seed capital under PMFME convergence is repayable as a loan with interest not exceeding 6% per annum
Funding for City Livelihood Centres and shelters is subject to availability and approval
Training under EST&P requires third-party certification and assessment
Shelter provision for urban homeless is to be achieved by 2022 as per guidelines
Innovative & Special Projects (I&SP) component limited to up to 5% of total central funds
